round: second candidate frame, first visual observations
source: Joshi and Parpola 1987, CISI1, official IGNCA scan
orientation: Lowercase photographs are seal impressions, in the normal right-to-left orientation; uppercase originals are mirrored relative to those impressions.

observations.source_constraints: The second graphic group from the left of the normalized impression lies between the jar-like form and an elongated fish-like form. A tall central/branched structure and lower diverging hooked strokes remain, with continuous surface above and below. The group appears spatially coherent and neither adjacent graphic is cut off by the damaged portion.
observations.caution: This identifies a bounded graphic motif with surviving carving, not a proven single linguistic sign. Fine graphic identity is withheld. Alternative catalogues may already identify it.

observations.source_constraints: Between the decorated diamond-like form and the rightmost complex graphic is one tall U-shaped graphic, with its left vertical edge, rounded lower join, right vertical edge and short upper attachment all visible. The immediate surrounding seal surface survives. It is substantially readable in both original and impression photographs.
observations.caution: The photograph does not show a physically lost glyph at this catalogue-unknown position. Any assigned code would be a transcription correction or recoding, not a restoration of absent text or a semantic decipherment. Alternative catalogue and sign inventory must be checked.

observations.source_constraints: The previous Mayig source audit rejected the same object. Broad internal spall remains compatible with multiple narrow units or a compound. One W000 does not independently establish one sign.

The right top portion of the original seal, and hence left end of the normalized impression, is broken and irregular. The photographs do not independently bound the full lost text span. The alternative impression marked bis is another photograph of the same side, not another artifact or a separate linguistic face.
This is a tablet rather than an original seal. Its two A photographs show extensive surface weathering and weak carving; a single bounded missing graphic cannot be established independently.
